  font-family: var(--font-display);
  letter-spacing: 0;
}

h1 {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 4.5rem;
  line-height: 1;
  text-wrap: balance;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.hero__tagline {
  max-width: 30rem;
  margin: 1.5rem 0 0;
  color: var(--colour-brand);
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: 2rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.15;
}

.hero__summary {
  max-width: 35rem;
  margin: 1.5rem 0 0;
  color: var(--colour-text-secondary);
  font-size: 1.125rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
}

.hero__brand-art {
  position: absolute;
  z-index: 1;
  right: max(1.5rem, calc((100vw - 100rem) / 2));
  bottom: -1rem;
  width: min(38vw, 31rem);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.hero__logo {
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}

.principles {
  padding-block: 5rem;
  background: var(--colour-surface);
}

.section-heading {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(8rem, 0.7fr) minmax(0, 2fr);
  align-items: end;
  gap: 2rem;
  padding-bottom: 2rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--colour-border);
}

.section-heading .eyebrow {
  margin: 0;
}

h2 {
  max-width: 18ch;
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 2.5rem;
  line-height: 1.1;
}

.principles__grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 2.5rem;
}

.principles article {
  padding-top: 2rem;
}

.principle-number {
  margin: 0 0 2rem;
  color: var(--colour-brand-text);
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  font-weight: 700;
}

h3 {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 1.5rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
}

.principles article p:last-child {
  max-width: 28ch;
  margin: 0.75rem 0 0;
  color: var(--colour-text-secondary);
  line-height: 1.6;
}

.site-footer {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--colour-border);
  background: var(--colour-surface-raised);
}

.site-footer__inner {
  min-height: 8rem;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 2rem;
}

.site-footer p {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--colour-text-secondary);
  font-size: 0.875rem;
}

@media (max-width: 56.25rem) {
  .hero__brand-art {
    right: -8rem;
    width: 26rem;
    opacity: 0.38;
  }

  .hero::before {
    left: 72%;
  }
}

@media (max-width: 39.9375rem) {
  .site-header__inner,
  .site-footer__inner,
  .content-boundary,
  .hero__content {
    width: min(100% - 1.5rem, 100rem);
  }

  .site-header__inner {
    min-height: 5rem;
    gap: 0.75rem;
  }

  .brand-wordmark {
    width: 8.75rem;
  }

  .theme-control {
    gap: 0.5rem;
  }

  .theme-control__label {
    position: absolute;
    width: 1px;
    height: 1px;
    overflow: hidden;
    clip: rect(0 0 0 0);
    clip-path: inset(50%);
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

  .theme-control__value {
    min-width: 0;
    max-width: 4.25rem;
    font-size: 0.75rem;
    line-height: 1.1;
  }

  .hero {
    min-height: 42rem;
  }

  .hero::before {
    display: none;
  }

  .hero::after {
    right: 0.75rem;
    bottom: 1rem;
    width: 4rem;
  }

  .hero__content {
    padding-block: 3.5rem 11rem;
  }

  h1 {
    max-width: 100%;
    font-size: 2.5rem;
  }

  .hero__tagline {
    max-width: 16rem;
    font-size: 1.625rem;
  }

  .hero__summary {
    max-width: 31rem;
    font-size: 1rem;
  }

  .hero__brand-art {
    right: -0.5rem;
    bottom: -1rem;
    width: 18rem;
    opacity: 0.8;
  }

  .principles {
    padding-block: 3.5rem;
  }

  .section-heading,
  .principles__grid {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }

  .section-heading {
    gap: 1rem;
  }

  h2 {
    font-size: 2rem;
  }

  .principles__grid {
    gap: 0;
  }

  .principles article {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 2.5rem minmax(0, 1fr);
    column-gap: 0.75rem;
    padding-block: 1.5rem;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--colour-border);
  }

  .principle-number {
    grid-row: 1 / span 2;
    margin: 0;
  }

  .principles article p:last-child {
    max-width: none;
  }

  .site-footer__inner {
    min-height: 9rem;
    align-items: flex-start;
    flex-direction: column;
    justify-content: center;
    gap: 1rem;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *,
  *::before,
  *::after {
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
  }
}

import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';

test('public landing page is responsive and supports persisted keyboard theme selection', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  const pageErrors: string[] = [];

  page.on('pageerror', (error) => {
    pageErrors.push(error.message);
  });

  await page.goto('/');

  await expect(
    page.getByRole('heading', {
      name: 'Stat’sTheGame',
    }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText('The game, measured ball by ball.').first()).toBeVisible();

  const themeToggle = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Switch to Night Match theme' });
  await themeToggle.focus();
  await expect(themeToggle).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');

  await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'night');
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => window.localStorage.getItem('statsthegame-theme'))).toBe(
    'night',
  );

  const hasHorizontalOverflow = await page.evaluate(
    () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth,
  );

  expect(hasHorizontalOverflow).toBe(false);
  expect(pageErrors).toEqual([]);
});

> Use an npm-workspace monorepo with separate deployable frontend and backend applications and a small shared contracts package.
  
  ```text
  Sport-Analytics-Tool/
  │   │   └── tests/
> │   └── frontend/
  │       ├── public/
  │       └── src/
  │           ├── api/
  │           ├── components/
> │           ├── features/
> │           ├── pages/
  │           └── test/
  ├── packages/
> │   └── contracts/
  ├── database/
  │   ├── migrations/
  │   ├── schema/
  
> 1. `apps/frontend` may communicate with `apps/backend` only through the documented HTTP API.
> 2. `apps/frontend` must not query application tables through Supabase-generated endpoints.
  3. `apps/backend` owns validation, authorisation, business rules, external integrations, and database access.
> 4. `packages/contracts` contains schemas and types only; it is not a third application or service.
  5. Database migrations are team-controlled and versioned under `database/migrations`.
  6. Cross-application end-to-end, performance, and accessibility tests live under `tests/`; unit and integration tests stay close to the application they 
test.
  7. Evidence files are records, not marketing claims. Store only genuine meetings, results, decisions, and contributions.
  
> The monorepo reduces setup overhead and supports coordinated changes, but the team must review Pull Requests for boundary violations. A shared 
repository does not make the application monolithic as long as the frontend and backend remain independent deployable applications with HTTP between them.

The issue is now sufficiently defined. #47, #58, and #59 are merged on `origin/main`, providing exact anonymous endpoints, public-only response schemas, supported filters, opaque cursor pagination, and machine-readable errors. The existing #89 shell/design system and merged #64 provider do not block anonymous pages; the public routes will sit inside the shell and will not consume auth state.

Plan:
1. Create `feat/48-public-browsing-pages` from the refreshed `origin/main`.
2. Add client routing and public API/schema adapters for competitions, seasons, fixtures, competitors, and participants.
3. Build list/detail pages with URL-backed filters, cursor navigation, cross-record links, and explicit loading, empty, not-found, and request-error states.
4. Extend the shared header navigation and responsive semantic styling without adding statistics, upload, account, or administrator behavior.
5. Add focused component/API tests plus anonymous desktop/mobile browser coverage, update only required frontend documentation and evidence, then run the full applicable checks.

The only interpretation needed is route naming; conventional plural resource routes matching #47 (`/competitions`, `/seasons`, `/fixtures`, `/competitors`, `/participants`, plus `/:id`) are directly supported by the documented contracts and do not require an invented backend contract. No genuine blocker remains.

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"

Frontend tests cover main states.
The implementation is reviewed through a Pull Request.

Public competition, fixture and participant read APIs.
Existing frontend application and design system.

# Dependencies

## Selection principles

A dependency must have a clear project purpose, an acceptable licence, active maintenance, security support, and a cost lower than implementing and maintaining the capability safely yourselves.

## Initial dependencies

| Area             | Dependency                         | Purpose                                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend         | React                              | Component-based web user interface                          |
| Frontend tooling | Vite                               | Development server and production build                     |
| Backend          | Express                            | Hand-written HTTP routing and middleware                    |
| Validation       | Zod                                | Runtime validation and TypeScript type derivation           |
| HTTP security    | Helmet                             | Secure response-header defaults                             |
| Logging          | Pino HTTP                          | Structured request logging foundation                       |
| Testing          | Vitest, Testing Library, Supertest | Component, unit, and API integration tests                  |
| Documentation    | MkDocs Material                    | Public static documentation website                         |
| Authentication   | `@supabase/supabase-js`            | Manage frontend sessions and validate backend access tokens |
| Configuration    | dotenv                             | Load ignored local backend environment files                |

## Review requirements

Before each milestone:

- review direct and transitive vulnerabilities;
- remove unused packages;
- document newly added third-party services and code;
- verify licences and attribution needs;
- record significant dependency decisions in an ADR; and
- retest the application after upgrades.

Exact installed versions are recorded in the committed `package-lock.json`. Use `npm ci` rather than `npm install` when validating a clean checkout or running CI.

## Authentication dependency review

The frontend uses the maintained `@supabase/supabase-js` client for managed browser sessions. The
backend uses the same library without browser persistence to validate access tokens through
Supabase Auth.

Dependency audit findings must be reviewed according to their actual dependency path and exploitability. Do not run `npm audit fix --force` without reviewing proposed breaking changes.

The team must monitor Supabase client releases and rerun `npm audit --omit=dev` during dependency reviews.

## TypeScript compatibility

TypeScript is pinned to version `5.5.4` because the current `@typescript-eslint` version supports TypeScript versions below `5.6.0`. TypeScript and `@typescript-eslint` should be reviewed and upgraded together.

## AI Declaration

The frontend authentication dependency documentation was updated with the assistance of
Codex[GPT-5.6 Sol].

# Dependencies

## Selection principles

A dependency must have a clear project purpose, an acceptable licence, active maintenance, security support, and a cost lower than implementing and maintaining the capability safely yourselves.

## Initial dependencies

| Area             | Dependency                         | Purpose                                                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend         | React                              | Component-based web user interface                          |
| Frontend tooling | Vite                               | Development server and production build                     |
| Backend          | Express                            | Hand-written HTTP routing and middleware                    |
| Validation       | Zod                                | Runtime validation and TypeScript type derivation           |
| HTTP security    | Helmet                             | Secure response-header defaults                             |
| Logging          | Pino HTTP                          | Structured request logging foundation                       |
| Testing          | Vitest, Testing Library, Supertest | Component, unit, and API integration tests                  |
| Documentation    | MkDocs Material                    | Public static documentation website                         |
| Authentication   | `@supabase/supabase-js`            | Manage frontend sessions and validate backend access tokens |
| Configuration    | dotenv                             | Load ignored local backend environment files                |

## Review requirements

Before each milestone:

- review direct and transitive vulnerabilities;
- remove unused packages;
- document newly added third-party services and code;
- verify licences and attribution needs;
- record significant dependency decisions in an ADR; and
- retest the application after upgrades.

Exact installed versions are recorded in the committed `package-lock.json`. Use `npm ci` rather than `npm install` when validating a clean checkout or running CI.

## Authentication dependency review

The frontend uses the maintained `@supabase/supabase-js` client for managed browser sessions. The
backend uses the same library without browser persistence to validate access tokens through
Supabase Auth.

Dependency audit findings must be reviewed according to their actual dependency path and exploitability. Do not run `npm audit fix --force` without reviewing proposed breaking changes.

The team must monitor Supabase client releases and rerun `npm audit --omit=dev` during dependency reviews.

## TypeScript compatibility

TypeScript is pinned to version `5.5.4` because the current `@typescript-eslint` version supports TypeScript versions below `5.6.0`. TypeScript and `@typescript-eslint` should be reviewed and upgraded together.

   1: # Public read API
   2: 
   3: The public read API provides anonymous access to competition and fixture reference data.
   4: 
   5: No sign-in or bearer token is required for these endpoints.
   6: 
   7: All application data is served through the handwritten Express backend. Supabase-generated Data API or PostgREST endpoints are not used as the public Sport Analytics API.
   8: 
   9: ## Base path
  10: 
  11: ```text
  12: /api/v1
  13: ```
  14: 
  15: ## Resources
  16: 
  17: The public API exposes:
  18: 
  19: - competitions;
  20: - seasons;
  21: - fixtures;
  22: - competitors; and
  23: - participants.
  24: 
  25: For cricket, competitors are teams and participants are people/players.
  26: 
  27: ## Competition endpoints
  28: 
  29: ```http
  30: GET /api/v1/competitions
  31: GET /api/v1/competitions/{competitionId}
  32: ```
  33: 
  34: Supported collection filter:
  35: 
  36: ```text
  37: name
  38: ```
  39: 
  40: Deterministic ordering:
  41: 
  42: ```text
  43: name ASC
  44: competitionId ASC
  45: ```
  46: 
  47: ## Season endpoints
  48: 
  49: ```http
  50: GET /api/v1/seasons
  51: GET /api/v1/seasons/{seasonId}
  52: ```
  53: 
  54: Supported collection filter:
  55: 
  56: ```text
  57: competitionId
  58: ```
  59: 
  60: A season resource is derived from a competition and the season value recorded on its fixtures.
  61: 
  62: `seasonId` is a stable opaque identifier derived by the backend. Consumers must not decode or derive meaning from its representation.
  63: 
  64: Deterministic ordering:
  65: 
  66: ```text
  67: competitionId ASC
  68: season ASC
  69: ```
  70: 
  71: ## Fixture endpoints
  72: 
  73: ```http
  74: GET /api/v1/fixtures
  75: GET /api/v1/fixtures/{fixtureId}
  76: ```
  77: 
  78: Supported collection filters:
  79: 
  80: ```text
  81: competitionId
  82: seasonId
  83: competitorId
  84: gender
  85: startDateFrom
  86: startDateTo
  87: ```
  88: 
  89: The date bounds are inclusive.
  90: 
  91: Example:
  92: 
  93: ```http
  94: GET /api/v1/fixtures?competitionId=12&competitorId=20&limit=25
  95: ```
  96: 
  97: Example response:
  98: 
  99: ```json
 100: {
 101:   "data": [
 102:     {
 103:       "fixtureId": "481",
 104:       "competitionId": "12",
 105:       "seasonId": "season_...",
 106:       "season": "2026",
 107:       "matchType": "T20",
 108:       "teamType": "international",
 109:       "gender": "male",
 110:       "ballsPerOver": 6,
 111:       "scheduledOvers": 20,
 112:       "startDate": "2026-08-09",
 113:       "endDate": "2026-08-09"
 114:     }
 115:   ],
 116:   "pagination": {
 117:     "nextCursor": null
 118:   }
 119: }
 120: ```
 121: 
 122: Deterministic fixture ordering:
 123: 
 124: ```text
 125: startDate ASC
 126: fixtureId ASC
 127: ```
 128: 
 129: ## Competitor endpoints
 130: 
 131: ```http
 132: GET /api/v1/competitors
 133: GET /api/v1/competitors/{competitorId}
 134: ```
 135: 
 136: Supported filters:
 137: 
 138: ```text
 139: competitionId
 140: seasonId
 141: name
 142: ```
 143: 
 144: A competitor represents a cricket team.
 145: 
 146: Deterministic ordering:
 147: 
 148: ```text
 149: name ASC
 150: competitorId ASC
 151: ```
 152: 
 153: ## Participant endpoints
 154: 
 155: ```http
 156: GET /api/v1/participants
 157: GET /api/v1/participants/{participantId}
 158: ```
 159: 
 160: Supported filters:
 161: 
 162: ```text
 163: fixtureId
 164: competitorId
 165: name
 166: ```
 167: 
 168: Only public participant fields are returned.
 169: 
 170: Internal source references, authentication data, submission records and audit information are not exposed.
 171: 
 172: Deterministic ordering:
 173: 
 174: ```text
 175: displayName ASC
 176: participantId ASC
 177: ```
 178: 
 179: ## Pagination
 180: 
 181: Collection endpoints use cursor pagination.
 182: 
 183: The default page size is:
 184: 
 185: ```text
 186: 50
 187: ```
 188: 
 189: The maximum page size is:
 190: 
 191: ```text
 192: 100
 193: ```
 194: 
 195: Example:
 196: 
 197: ```http
 198: GET /api/v1/competitions?limit=25
 199: ```
 200: 
 201: A response may contain:
 202: 
 203: ```json
 204: {
 205:   "pagination": {
 206:     "nextCursor": "opaque-next-cursor"
 207:   }
 208: }
 209: ```
 210: 
 211: The next request can use:
 212: 
 213: ```http
 214: GET /api/v1/competitions?limit=25&cursor=opaque-next-cursor
 215: ```
 216: 
 217: Cursors and resource identifiers are opaque. Consumers must not derive meaning from their representation.
 218: 
 219: ## Not-found responses
 220: 
 221: Unknown resource identifiers return HTTP `404`.
 222: 
 223: Example:
 224: 
 225: ```json
 226: {
 227:   "error": {
 228:     "code": "NOT_FOUND",
 229:     "message": "Competition not found."
 230:   }
 231: }
 232: ```
 233: 
 234: ## Invalid requests
 235: 
 236: Invalid filters, page sizes or cursors return HTTP `400` using the shared machine-readable API error format.
 237: 
 238: ## OpenAPI
 239: 
 240: The machine-readable specification is documented in the [OpenAPI specification](openapi.md).
